name: Tet (Vietnamese New Year)
when: 27 January-3 February 2027 region: Tet day 6 February 2027, 26 January 2028; the break is about a week
summary: Vietnam's biggest holiday: families travel home, many shops close for days, and cities fill with flowers and lights.
details: The lunar new year, falling on the same day as Chinese New Year. In the days before, flower streets and markets open; on Tet itself many restaurants and shops are closed and transport is full. The length of the official break is set each year by the government.
crowd: Travel peaks at both ends of the break; trains and flights sell out.
price: Hotels and flights rise sharply; some places close.
perk: Flower streets, lion dances and fireworks in the main cities.

highlights.name: Hanoi (Hoan Kiem Lake and the flower market)
highlights.note: Flower market and fireworks around the lake.

highlights.name: Ho Chi Minh City (Nguyen Hue flower street)
highlights.note: Flower street along Nguyen Hue walking street.

highlights.name: Hoi An
highlights.note: Lanterns and lion dances in the old town.

name: National Day (Independence Day)
when: 2 September, nationwide (the break around it is set each year)
summary: Vietnam's National Day marks the 1945 Declaration of Independence; Hanoi has a ceremony at Ba Dinh Square.
details: Celebrated on 2 September with a parade or ceremony at Ba Dinh Square, fireworks and concerts. The holiday often runs a day or more beyond the 2nd, depending on that year's announcement. Reunification Day, 30 April, is a separate holiday.
crowd: Domestic travel is heavy over the long weekend.
